name: Autoclave
label: Dischord
lede: Christina Billotte and Mary Timony wrote for the same band for about a year, played roughly fifteen shows, and left one 7" behind before they split for four cities.

eras.title: Two guitarists walk into Hazmat
eras.text: Christina Billotte and Melissa Berkoff had a rhythm section and no band. Nikki Chapman and Mary Timony, a college student in Boston who came down on her breaks, supplied the guitars, and the result was knotty, poppy and not much like anything else on Dischord.

years.p: [[Christina Billotte|62325e5d-014f-42a1-90d5-fa12e17aa214]], late of the Chrisbald 96, teams up with drummer Melissa Berkoff in a DC band called Hazmat.

years.h: Timony and Chapman join, and Hazmat turns into Autoclave
years.p: [[Mary Timony|d9c8dc3c-15b8-40d5-8153-ae9214aeef55]] and [[Nikki Chapman|c195e1c6-941b-41db-9ff3-2233f56ce93b]] add guitars while Billotte takes lead vocals and bass. Bandcamp Daily later described it as two "generational" talents in one band.
years.xp: Dischord dates the band from summer 1990. Bandcamp Daily called the songs "knotty yet poppy" and heard "inspired amateurism and clever technical twists", with Timony's guitar playing against Billotte's singing.

years.h: Autoclave at the Middle East, Cambridge, before any record exists
years.p: The Todestrieb archive logs this set as their Boston show. No Autoclave record is out yet, and Timony is still in school in town.
years.xp: Todestrieb's write-up, headed "30 Years Ago", puts the band on the Middle East stage on November 25, 1990. Timony was in college in Boston and played with the band on her breaks.

years.h: Their first tour goes out with Fugazi and Beat Happening
years.p: Timony, recalling Autoclave's first tour, which she did alongside Fugazi and Beat Happening.
years.xp: Todestrieb quotes Timony on it: "Our first tour was with Fugazi and Beat Happening. I was a lucky kid!" The year isn't stated, and it could be 1991 rather than 1990.

eras.title: One 7", then May
eras.text: While they were a band, Autoclave put out a single 7", Go Far. Dischord's own line is that they defied classification and context, and they were done by May.

years.h: Go Far comes out on Dischord and K
years.p: Three songs on Dischord No. 60.5, a joint release with Olympia's K Records, under the DisKord banner. Bandcamp Daily heard inspired amateurism meeting clever technical twists.

years.h: Four members leave for four cities
years.p: Christina Billotte's count of the band's total. Autoclave end in May 1991: Nikki Chapman to Olympia, Melissa Berkoff to New Orleans, Mary Timony to Boston, Billotte stays in DC.
years.xp:
Billotte has described Autoclave as together off and on for two years, while Dischord's dates run from summer 1990 to May 1991. Either way the run was short.

Bandcamp Daily's version: they parted ways in 1991, the year punk broke.

eras.title: Two bands, two cities, one record later
eras.text: Most people heard Autoclave after it was over. Timony built Helium in Boston, Billotte built Slant 6 in DC, and the rest of Autoclave's music came out behind them.

years.h: A 10" EP arrives a year after the split
years.p: Autoclave's second and last record comes out on Mira and Dischord in 1992.
years.xp: Mira is Billotte's own label. Dischord calls it a posthumous 10".

years.h: Timony starts Helium in Boston, Billotte starts Slant 6 in DC
years.p: Billotte later adds [[Quix*o*tic|e4ad9a5b-7358-46be-9d34-73e9b9d072ec]] and [[The Casual Dots|d74e8159-d217-4a24-8ef0-5c2aab85a308]]. Timony has called Slant 6 one of her all-time favourite groups.
years.xp: Todestrieb quotes Billotte: "I wanted to do something more straightforward than Autoclave, more danceable." Slant 6's first 7" followed in early 1994, per Bandcamp Daily.

years.h: Dischord collects everything on one CD
years.p: Dischord No. 108 has eleven tracks: both EPs, a song from the Simple Machines Lever 7", and the live favorite Paper Boy, a cover of the Paperboy video game theme.
years.xp: Barrett Jones engineered and produced, with further recording by [[Geoff Turner|591fc466-2668-4524-852d-a6cc5f18cff7]] and [[Alec Bourgeois|9de67d7e-bc5a-47fc-a00f-073d6e0519cb]]; [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] of Fugazi mixed. Maximum Rocknroll heard Christina Billotte's basslines as close to Wire, and praised her voice outright.

eras.title: Pressed again, found again
eras.text: Autoclave never reunited, but the collected recordings keep getting repressed, and each time a new set of listeners shows up.

years.p: Dischord and Mira reissue the Autoclave CD, remastered at Silver Sonya.

years.h: Finally on vinyl, scoring 8.6 at Pitchfork
years.p: The collected recordings come out as an LP. Bandcamp Daily calls it a key indie text; Wikipedia lists Pitchfork's score as 8.6.

sources.title: Bandcamp Daily: A Guide to Christina Billotte
